channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan's tenge weakens against dollar due to external factors
item.description: The Association of Financiers attributes the tenge's sharp decline to falling oil prices and a strengthening dollar globally. Increased demand for dollars from Kazakh citizens may also have contributed. The dollar reached 451.50 tenge, a significant rise after weeks of tenge appreciation.

item.title: Tajikistan modernizes seismic stations with new digital equipment
item.description: Tajikistan is upgrading its seismic stations with new digital equipment as part of a modernization program. New equipment has been installed at the Boghidzhugda and Sarband stations. This initiative, supported by the World Bank, aims to enhance seismic data analysis and risk assessment capabilities.

item.title: Head of Court in Kazakhstan's Kyzylorda Region Sentenced to 9 Years for Corruption
item.description: The head of a court and a judge in Kazakhstan's Kyzylorda region have been sentenced to nine years in prison for corruption offenses, the National Security Committee (KNB) reported. They were found guilty of accepting a large bribe, with the judge allegedly receiving 6 million tenge to grant a suspended sentence to a fraudster, and an additional 300,000 tenge for full release.

item.title: Iran Envoy: Afghanistan and Iran Share Common Opportunities and Threats
item.description: Iran's deputy ambassador in Kabul, Seyed Hassan Mortazavi, stated that Iran and Afghanistan face shared opportunities and threats due to current regional and global developments. He emphasized the need for close cooperation to address common challenges and safeguard mutual interests, including security, economic matters, and border cooperation.

item.title: Former Kazaly District Court Chairman and Judge Sentenced for Bribery
item.description: The former chairman and a judge of the Kazaly District Court in the Kyzylorda region have been sentenced to nine years in prison each. The National Security Committee reported they were found guilty of corruption offenses, including accepting large bribes. They were apprehended in January.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Oil Industry Successfully Postpones Fuel Excise Tax Increase
item.description: Kazakhstan's oil industry, through the PetroMining Association, has convinced the government to postpone the planned increase in excise taxes on petroleum products. The increase, which would have raised rates from 50% to 95% of the price difference, is now delayed from January 1, 2027.

item.title: Daurenbek Yryskali Appointed President of "Otanadastar" Fund
item.description: Daurenbek Yryskali has been appointed president of the "Otanadastar" Fund, according to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Kazakhstan. Born in 1963, Yryskali has held various diplomatic positions since 1993, including consul general in Omsk and counselor-envoy in Germany.

item.title: Iranian Oil Minister Mohsen Khojastehmehr Resigns; Hamid Bovard Appointed Acting Minister
item.description: Iranian Oil Minister Mohsen Khojastehmehr resigned on October 4 for personal reasons, which President Masoud Pezeshkian eventually accepted. Hamid Bovard, formerly deputy oil minister, has been appointed acting oil minister. Khojastehmehr had served since August 2024.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rakhmon Calls for Increased Use of Tajik Language Online
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rakhmon has urged for the expanded use of the Tajik language, particularly on the internet, in a message for State Language Day. He emphasized the language's role in national identity, culture, and unity, noting its development over 35 years of independence. The president highlighted government initiatives, including laws and programs, aimed at strengthening the language's status.

item.title: Court Chairman and Judge Sentenced to Nine Years for Corruption in Kazakhstan's Kyzylorda Region
item.description: The chairman and a judge of the Kazalinsky District Court in Kazakhstan's Kyzylorda region have been sentenced to nine years in prison for corruption offenses. They were found guilty of accepting large bribes. The arrests were made in January 2026, and the verdict was delivered on September 18, 2026, according to the National Security Committee.

item.title: Kazakhstan Appoints First Deputy Defense Minister and Chief of General Staff
item.description: Aitkurban Omarbekov has been appointed First Deputy Minister of Defense and Chief of the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Kazakhstan. He was relieved of his previous duties. Azamat Khasenov was appointed Deputy Head of the State Security Service and Commander of Special Forces. Azamat Yeskarayev, former Minister of Justice, became Head of the State Legal Department of the Presidential Administration.

item.title: Kazakhstan Continues Transportation Infrastructure Modernization with Road and Rail Upgrades
item.description: Kazakhstan is modernizing its transport infrastructure, with 19,100 km of roads reconstructed or repaired by 2025. By the end of 2026, 95% of national and 92% of local roads are planned to meet standards. Over the past five years, 911 km of new railway were built, with another 800 km under construction.

item.title: New Industrial, Transport, and Energy Facilities Opened Across Kazakhstan Regions
item.description: New industrial enterprises, transport hubs, and energy facilities have been launched across Kazakhstan. In the Almaty region, a new non-alcoholic beverage plant created 230 jobs. A long-shelf-life bread and confectionery factory began operations in North Kazakhstan, utilizing modern European equipment. The Kokshetau railway station was also modernized.

item.title: Kazakhstan Enhances Border Controls Amid Suspected Plague Cases in Russia
item.description: Kazakhstan has intensified border surveillance due to concerns over potential plague infections originating from Russia. This measure follows reports of suspected plague cases within Russia, prompting Kazakhstan to implement stricter controls to prevent any possible spread across its borders.

item.title: Kazakhstan Strengthens Preventive Measures as Russia Reports Suspected Plague Cases
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Health is monitoring the situation in Russia's Irkutsk region, where a 28-year-old woman working at a plague research institute has died under suspicion of contracting the disease. While one theory suggests a lab accident, official confirmation is pending. Kazakhstan is enhancing its own preventive measures.

item.title: Economist: Traffic Congestion in Uzbekistan is a State Policy Issue Requiring Solutions
item.description: Economist Islombek Niyozmetov stated that traffic congestion in Uzbekistan's cities, particularly Tashkent, has become a significant problem. He emphasized that traffic is not merely an inconvenience but a critical issue that requires attention at the state policy level, necessitating comprehensive solutions to address its socio-economic impacts.

item.title: Kaspi.kz CEO Demonstrates AI Assistant Kasper to Prime Minister in Astana
item.description: At the Digital Bridge forum in Astana, Kaspi.kz CEO Mikhail Lomtadze showcased Kasper, an AI assistant designed to help customers choose products based on their needs. Kasper analyzes preferences, reviews, and characteristics, offering personalized recommendations and comparisons in multiple languages.

item.title: UNESCO Calls for Increased Support for Teachers on World Teachers' Day
item.description: On World Teachers' Day, UNESCO urged greater support and improved professional status for teachers globally. The organization highlighted challenges like digital technologies, climate change, and migration, emphasizing the need for better working conditions and recognition for effective role performance.

item.title: Astana Considers Public Transport Fare Increase to 150 Tenge, Social Benefits to Remain
item.description: Astana's city administration has proposed increasing public transport fares to 150 tenge for non-cash payments, effective December 1. The current fare of 110 tenge has been in place since 2014, with costs for fuel, driver salaries, and parts significantly rising. Social benefits for eligible categories will be preserved.

item.title: Tajikistan Plans 800 MW "Khutalon" Hydroelectric Power Station Construction
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Energy and Water Resources visited the planned site for the "Khutalon" (Shurob) hydroelectric power station. The facility, with a projected capacity of 800 MW and an annual output exceeding 2.5 billion kWh, will be built on the Vakhsh River between the Rogun and Nurek HPPs. The project aims to increase the country's energy generation capacity and optimize hydropower resource utilization.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Health Ministry Assesses Low Risk of Infection Import from Russia
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Health is monitoring the situation in Russia's Irkutsk region, stating that preventative measures are in place. Border control includes sanitary-quarantine checks, with no individuals showing symptoms of dangerous infections detected. The ministry assures the risk of infection import remains low, while awaiting official confirmation on the situation in Irkutsk.

item.title: Former Justice Minister Azamat Yeskarayev Appointed Head of Legal Department in Kazakhstan's Presidential Administration
item.description: Former Minister of Justice Azamat Yeskarayev has been appointed head of the state-legal department of the Presidential Administration of Kazakhstan. Previously, Yeskarayev served as ambassador to India and several other South Asian countries. He also held positions in the Prime Minister's office and was the Minister of Justice from 2023 until his recent appointment.

item.title: Kazakh Defense Minister Conducts Surprise Inspection of Military Unit in Akmola Garrison
item.description: Kazakh Defense Minister Aidarbekov conducted a surprise inspection at a military unit in the Akmola garrison. He reviewed troop organization, living conditions, and the unit's material and technical base, focusing on barracks and infrastructure. The minister issued directives to improve soldiers' living conditions.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Suspend Increased Fuel Excise Taxes from 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan will suspend increased excise tax rates on petroleum products for wholesale suppliers starting in 2027. The PetroMining Association stated that the previously raised rate of 95% would harm the economy of subsoil users. The government decided to suspend the measure after risks were presented by the association and oil producers.

item.title: Russian Tank Crews Practice Engaging Simulated Enemy in Tajikistan Drills
item.description: Russian tank crews of the T-72B3M variant successfully engaged simulated targets during the 'Center-2026' strategic command and staff exercises in Tajikistan. The drills took place on the 'Lyaur' mountain training ground, utilizing terrain for cover and employing tactics like 'fire carousel'.

item.title: UN Official Discusses Governance, Regional Peace, and Migrant Return with Afghan Deputy Minister
item.description: Rosemary DiCarlo, UN Under-Secretary-General for Political and Peacebuilding Affairs, met with Afghanistan’s Deputy Minister of Urban Development and Housing in Kabul. Discussions covered governance, regional stability, housing, Afghan migrant return, and Afghanistan-Pakistan transit routes. DiCarlo affirmed the UN's continued support for the Afghan people.

item.title: Tax Inspectors in Qashqadaryo Accused of Embezzling Over 122 Million Soums
item.description: Tax inspection employees in Qarshi city, Qashqadaryo region, have been exposed for embezzling funds from taxpayers. According to the Department for Combating Economic Crimes under the General Prosecutor's Office, nine tax inspectors allegedly accepted 122.6 million soums from 97 taxpayers, failing to credit the funds to their accounts and instead misappropriating them. A criminal case has been initiated.

item.title: Human Rights Watch: US Should Provide Reparations to Victims of 20-Year War in Afghanistan
item.description: Human Rights Watch is calling on the United States to provide reparations and accountability for victims of the 20-year war in Afghanistan. The organization stated that the US has a responsibility to address the harm caused by its military actions and policies during the conflict. This call comes amid ongoing discussions about the future of Afghanistan and the international community's role.

item.title: OPEC+ maintains Kazakhstan's oil production quota for November
item.description: The OPEC+ group has decided not to alter Kazakhstan's oil production quota for the month of November. This decision was made during the latest meeting of the alliance, which coordinates oil output among member countries. Kazakhstan's production levels will remain unchanged as per the agreement.

item.title: Kazakh President reshuffles military leadership after 14 soldiers' deaths
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev continues to reshuffle the military leadership following the deaths of 14 servicemen. New appointments include Aytkurman Omarbekov as Chief of the General Staff and First Deputy Minister of Defense, and Azamat Khasenov as Deputy Head of the State Security Service. Several other high-ranking officers were dismissed.

item.title: Tokayev appoints new Chief of General Staff of the Armed Forces
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has appointed Aytkurman Omarbekov as the new First Deputy Minister of Defense and Chief of the General Staff of the Armed Forces. Omarbekov previously served in the State Security Service. Azamat Khasenov was appointed as the new Deputy Head of the State Security Service. This follows recent dismissals of several high-ranking military officials.

item.title: Azamat Yeskarayev Appointed to Presidential Administration
item.description: Azamat Yeskarayev has been relieved of his duties as Kazakhstan's ambassador to India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Maldives, and Nepal. He has been appointed to a position within the Presidential Administration. Previously, he served as the Minister of Justice.

item.title: ADB Allocates $20.5 Million for Tajikistan's Pension Sector Amid Middle East Tensions
item.description: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has approved $20.5 million in financial assistance for Tajikistan's pension and social services sector. This funding, part of ADB's support for countries affected by Middle East economic and financial tensions, aims to improve pension services, modernize payment systems, and enhance social assistance accessibility.

item.title: First Group of Uzbek Citizens Sent to Italy for Seasonal Work; Medical Cooperation Expands
item.description: For the first time, a group of Uzbek citizens has been sent to Italy for seasonal employment. Cooperation in the medical field is also expanding, with plans to train nearly 20 highly educated nurses for work in Milan by the end of the year.

item.title: Iranian General Claims No U.S. Vessels Present in Persian Gulf or Northern Indian Ocean
item.description: An Iranian general claimed that no U.S. vessels are currently in the Persian Gulf, Strait of Hormuz, Gulf of Oman, or northern Indian Ocean. He asserted that American forces have withdrawn over 1,000 kilometers from Iran's borders, stating this is the first time in history the Persian Gulf is free of U.S. ships.

item.title: Suspect Arrested in Dushanbe for Fraudulent Medical College Admissions Scheme
item.description: Police in Dushanbe have arrested a 44-year-old man suspected of fraud, involving promises of assistance with medical college admissions and document processing. The suspect allegedly took money from victims without fulfilling his promises. Four cases related to medical college admissions are confirmed.

item.title: German Chancellor Visits Kyiv, Pledges Continued Support Amid Winter Concerns
item.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz arrived in Kyiv for an unannounced visit, pledging continued support for Ukraine as winter approaches. Accompanied by economic officials and entrepreneurs, Merz stated that stopping Russia is crucial for European security. Germany is preparing a new aid package worth 1.35 billion euros, including 1 billion for armaments and 350 million for energy security.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Outlines Strategic Priorities for Next Decade on Independence Day
item.description: On Uzbekistan's 35th Independence Day, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev presented key achievements and strategic goals for the coming decade. He highlighted historical transformations, economic growth reaching $160 billion GDP, poverty reduction to 4%, and increased access to education and healthcare, emphasizing human dignity and national values.

item.title: Horrific murder in Ghor: Nuria burned with a hot iron in front of her children and killed
item.description: A horrific murder occurred in Ghor province where a woman named Nuria was brutally killed. She was reportedly burned with a hot iron in front of her children before being murdered. Details surrounding the incident are still emerging.

item.title: UN highlights need for adequate housing for Afghan returnees on World Habitat Day
item.description: The United Nations stated that the need for adequate housing in Afghanistan has increased due to the rising number of Afghan returnees. The UN noted that current support is insufficient to meet the needs of these returnees, emphasizing the theme of "Adequate Housing for All" for this year's World Habitat Day.
